steps.title: Confirm the first-release hypotheses and access patterns
steps.summary: From September to December 2026, test the current hypothesis for the September 2027 release: King’s Edge as the deep native domain, with timetabling, KEATS and the student-enquiry gateway represented through the simplest safe and useful access patterns. Discovery can refine the precise mix before scope is locked.

outputs.title: First-release hypothesis assessment
outputs.summary: Record the student value, feasible access pattern, owner and material constraints for King’s Edge, timetabling, KEATS and the student-enquiry gateway.

outputs.title: Initial September scope
outputs.summary: Define the working first-release hypothesis without converting it into an irreversible commitment before discovery.

existingCapacity.owner: Digital and IT with the Digital Student Experience Hub mobilisation lead
existingCapacity.contribution: Confirm available interfaces and the simplest viable access pattern for each candidate first-release journey.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: The team may over-engineer the first release or discover constraints too late.

existingCapacity.owner: King’s Edge, timetabling, KEATS and enquiry-management owners
existingCapacity.contribution: Provide documentation, available interfaces, planned changes and named decision makers.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: The Hub may be designed around incorrect assumptions.

enablingConditions.condition: Keep King’s Edge as the fixed first deep native product domain. Treat timetabling, KEATS and the student-enquiry gateway as leading hypotheses whose exact first-release depth remains subject to discovery.
enablingConditions.owner: Digital Student Experience Hub mobilisation lead
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The first release may become overcommitted before feasibility and student value are understood.

steps.title: Map the wider digital estate and priority student journeys
steps.summary: From November 2026 to June 2027, undertake broad discovery across the student-facing digital estate, priority journeys, information flows, ownership, authoritative information, integration readiness and rationalisation opportunities. Include a small paid student visioning and co-design internship cohort to create a student-led vision and design principles, while wider research tests representativeness. Produce the evidence-led wider-Hub backlog without widening the first-release build.

outputs.title: Student-facing digital-estate map
outputs.summary: Map material systems, portals, channels and entry points and the relationships between them.

outputs.title: Student vision and co-design synthesis
outputs.summary: Use the paid internship cohort to produce a documented student vision for the Hub, experience/design principles, priority needs and tensions, prototype recommendations and a clear record of where student priorities challenge institutional assumptions.

outputs.title: Priority journey and service evidence
outputs.summary: Map selected current-state journeys and develop target service blueprints where deeper understanding is needed.

outputs.title: Information architecture and ownership principles
outputs.summary: Identify navigation, authoritative-information, content-ownership and governance requirements for a coherent Hub.

outputs.title: Integration and rationalisation readiness assessment
outputs.summary: Assess where data, APIs, service readiness and replacement confidence support deeper integration or later rationalisation.

outputs.title: Evidence-led wider-Hub backlog
outputs.summary: Prioritise candidate Year Two and Year Three journeys based on student need, value, readiness and delivery effort.

existingCapacity.owner: Existing or seconded institutional capability, organisational home to be confirmed
existingCapacity.contribution: Lead cross-service journey and service mapping alongside the product team.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: The broader Hub roadmap may be shaped by system opportunity rather than student journeys.

existingCapacity.owner: Existing or seconded institutional capability, organisational home to be confirmed
existingCapacity.contribution: Map systems, information flows, ownership, dependencies and operational implications.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: Critical estate and dependency evidence may remain incomplete.

existingCapacity.owner: Existing or seconded institutional capability, organisational home to be confirmed
existingCapacity.contribution: Provide proportionate wider student research across priority journeys, validate emerging priorities and test whether findings from the paid internship cohort hold across a broader and more varied student population.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: The roadmap may lack credible student evidence.

existingCapacity.owner: Relevant faculties, SED services and Digital and IT
existingCapacity.contribution: Provide process, content, system, data and ownership evidence and participate in target-state design.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: The discovery may describe the estate without establishing viable ownership or change routes.

newInvestment.item: Paid student visioning and co-design internships
newInvestment.estimatedCost: Indicative £15,000 Year One envelope in constant 2026 prices for a small cohort of short paid student internships. Treat this as the total employment envelope, including any relevant payroll/on-cost treatment, until King’s employment arrangements are confirmed.
newInvestment.owner: Digital Student Experience Hub mobilisation lead
newInvestment.fundingRoute: Year One Digital Student Experience Hub mobilisation business case
newInvestment.rationale: Creates sustained, paid student participation in visioning and co-design rather than relying only on occasional consultation. The cohort should shape the Hub vision, challenge institutional assumptions, contribute to prototypes and design principles, and generate reusable discovery evidence. It complements rather than replaces broader representative research.
newInvestment.riskIfMissing: Student participation may become episodic and consultative, reducing the depth of student influence over the emerging Hub proposition and first-release experience.

enablingConditions.condition: Broad discovery must remain protected from first-release delivery pressure and must not automatically widen the first-release build.
enablingConditions.owner: Digital Student Experience Hub mobilisation lead
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: Either the evidence base or the focused September release will be compromised.

enablingConditions.condition: Recruit the paid internship cohort for diversity of experience and be explicit that it is a co-design group rather than a representative sample; use wider research to validate and challenge its findings.
enablingConditions.owner: Digital Student Experience Hub mobilisation lead with user-research support
enablingConditions.decisionNeededBy: Before internship recruitment and throughout interpretation of findings
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: A small cohort may be over-interpreted as representative of the wider student population.

steps.title: Establish the shared app architecture and platform foundations
steps.summary: From November 2026 to February 2027, establish the minimum bespoke Hub architecture, hosting, identity, navigation, orchestration, telemetry and service foundations needed for the King’s Edge replatform and focused first release.

outputs.title: Bespoke Hub architecture blueprint
outputs.summary: Define the student-facing aggregation, orchestration and intelligence-layer boundary for the first release and future growth.

outputs.title: Shared application foundations
outputs.summary: Establish hosting, identity, common shell, navigation, telemetry, assurance and live-service patterns needed by Edge and the Hub.

existingCapacity.contribution: Provide architecture authority, Azure and DevOps expertise, identity design and platform engineering.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: The Edge replatform and Hub may lack an agreed, supportable foundation.

existingCapacity.owner: Digital and IT with Student Systems and Data
existingCapacity.contribution: Advise on authoritative sources, available interfaces, security, privacy and accessibility. The focused first release must not wait for the wider Student Systems and Data programme to complete.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: The team may create avoidable coupling or unsafe interfaces.

newInvestment.item: Year 1 Digital Student Experience Hub Azure, environments and platform costs
newInvestment.estimatedCost: £50,000 Year One planning envelope in constant 2026 prices. Earlier detailed Year One costing was approximately £40,000, so this retains a modest contingency without carrying forward the previous £90,000 placeholder.
newInvestment.fundingRoute: Year One Digital Student Experience Hub mobilisation business case
newInvestment.rationale: Funds Azure, environments and core platform costs for the focused first release with reasonable contingency. Agentic software-development tooling is explicitly excluded from this envelope and is treated separately as an unvalidated option under 4.1.3.
newInvestment.riskIfMissing: The shared app foundations and Edge replatform may lack the platform services needed for safe operation.

enablingConditions.condition: Keep the £50,000 Year One platform envelope under review against actual Azure and environment consumption; do not treat unused contingency as automatic budget for unrelated tooling or specialist staffing.
enablingConditions.decisionNeededBy: At platform mobilisation and through Year One
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The platform budget may drift away from actual consumption or become a catch-all for unrelated costs.

steps.title: Prototype the common student home
steps.summary: From November 2026 to April 2027, test increasingly realistic versions of the shared home with students, using the paid co-design internship cohort for sustained visioning and design work and wider student research for validation. Focus on information hierarchy, navigation, the relationship between King’s Edge and lighter-touch institutional journeys, and whether the Hub is genuinely useful as a starting point.

outputs.title: Co-designed common student-home prototypes
outputs.summary: Develop and test progressively realistic versions of the shared home with the paid co-design cohort, then validate key assumptions with a broader student population.

outputs.title: Evidence-led build refinements
outputs.summary: Translate proportionate student testing into a focused first-release backlog.

existingCapacity.contribution: Design the shared student experience and work with reliable user-research support to test it.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: The Hub may become a set of links without a coherent experience.

steps.title: Build the shared Hub shell alongside King’s Edge
steps.summary: From January to June 2027, build the common home, identity, navigation, profile, orchestration and telemetry while the deeper King’s Edge product develops under 4.1.4. Implement only the timetable, KEATS and student-enquiry gateway access justified for the focused first release.

outputs.title: Reusable Hub shell
outputs.summary: Build the common home, navigation, profile, orchestration and telemetry.

outputs.title: Deep King’s Edge entry
outputs.summary: Place the substantive Edge experience within the shared student-home structure.

outputs.title: Focused institutional access
outputs.summary: Implement the useful timetable, KEATS and enquiry-gateway access supported by discovery.

existingCapacity.contribution: Build the common shell and focused service routes alongside the King’s Edge roadmap.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: Hub work may stall or displace committed Edge delivery.

enablingConditions.condition: Any proposed deeper non-Edge integration must make its capacity trade-off against King’s Edge explicit and be supported by evidence.
enablingConditions.owner: Digital Student Experience Hub mobilisation lead and 4.1.3 product leadership
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The wider Hub ambition may silently consume Edge capacity.

steps.title: Test the working Hub with students and service owners
steps.summary: From March to June 2027, test the working common home with a bounded but varied student cohort and relevant service owners, focusing on usefulness, task success, clarity, accessibility and hand-offs.

outputs.title: Working student-home test
outputs.summary: Use real product evidence to refine navigation, content and hand-offs without widening scope.

outputs.title: Initial task-success and ease-of-use measures
outputs.summary: Define how first-release baseline measures will be captured after launch.

steps.title: Lock the September first-release scope and Year Two priorities
steps.summary: By the end of June 2027, use product testing and the broader discovery evidence to confirm the minimum September release and an evidence-led priority backlog for the next phase.

outputs.title: September scope lock
outputs.summary: Confirm the shared home, substantive King’s Edge domain and the agreed additional first-release access patterns.

outputs.title: Evidence-led Year Two backlog
outputs.summary: Confirm the highest-value candidate journeys for deeper post-launch discovery and delivery.

steps.title: Complete proportionate launch readiness
steps.summary: During July and August 2027, complete security, privacy, accessibility, performance, monitoring, support and release-readiness work appropriate to the confirmed first-release scope while protecting King’s Edge service continuity.

outputs.title: Launch-ready first release
outputs.summary: Complete proportionate assurance and support checks for the confirmed Digital Student Experience Hub release.

steps.title: Launch the first Digital Student Experience Hub release
steps.summary: Launch in September 2027 with a coherent shared student home, King’s Edge as the substantive native product domain, and the agreed useful access to the other first-release journeys confirmed through discovery.

outputs.title: September 2027 first live release
outputs.summary: Make the Digital Student Experience Hub available to students with the confirmed focused scope.

outputs.title: Live evidence baseline
outputs.summary: Establish baseline evidence for active use, successful completion of priority tasks, perceived ease of use, hand-off performance and first-time journey success.

steps.title: Operate, learn and decide where deeper integration is worth it
steps.summary: From September 2027 to February 2028, use live evidence alongside Year One discovery to improve the Hub, establish baseline measures and identify where deeper integration would create enough student value to justify additional product, service and technical effort.

outputs.title: Post-launch evidence review
outputs.summary: Assess usage, task success, ease of use, hand-offs, technical performance and support evidence.

outputs.title: Costed next-phase options
outputs.summary: Use evidence to cost the next product, platform and integration needs within the three-year strategic investment envelope.

enablingConditions.condition: Future platform, integration and delivery costs must be costed from live evidence and the approved roadmap rather than carried forward as assumed annual envelopes.
enablingConditions.owner: Digital Student Experience Hub governance with Digital and IT and Finance
enablingConditions.decisionNeededBy: Before Year Two investment is committed
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: Later investment may become detached from the evidence-led mobilisation model.

steps.title: Approve the deeper roadmap and first end-to-end non-Edge journeys
steps.summary: From March to April 2028, combine live Hub evidence, the wider digital-estate and journey discovery, and learning from King’s Edge to select the first non-Edge areas that should move beyond access and hand-off into deeper integrated journeys.

outputs.title: Approved deeper-journey roadmap
outputs.summary: Select the first non-Edge end-to-end journeys based on student value, service readiness, data/integration readiness and cost.

steps.title: Deepen the Hub with the first end-to-end non-Edge journeys
steps.summary: Build the first selected deeper journeys into the existing Hub, connecting authoritative data and CRM-enabled interactions where ready while retaining specialist source systems where they continue to add value.

outputs.title: First deeper non-Edge journeys
outputs.summary: Deliver selected end-to-end journeys with appropriate data, service and CRM integration.

enablingConditions.condition: The depth and pace of these journeys are determined by authoritative data, APIs, integration routes, service readiness and the maturity of the Student Relationship and CRM Foundation.
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The programme may commit to journey depth that its dependencies cannot safely support.

enablingConditions.condition: Detailed Year Two and Year Three drawdown from the strategic investment envelope must be approved from evidence and costed delivery plans.
enablingConditions.owner: Digital Student Experience Hub governance with Finance
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The £3m mobilisation envelope may be treated as an automatic spend plan rather than a controlled strategic envelope.

steps.title: Expand integrated journeys and common Hub capabilities
steps.summary: Add further priority journeys and mature common search, actions, communications, notifications, personalisation, self-service and system integration, progressively replacing shallow hand-offs where deeper integration adds clear value.

outputs.title: Expanded integrated journey portfolio
outputs.summary: Increase the breadth and depth of journeys coherently accessible through the Hub.

steps.title: Make wider student journeys the primary product roadmap
steps.summary: By the end of the three-year mobilisation, establish the Hub as a broad institutional product with a substantial range of integrated journeys, mature governance and an evidence-led ongoing roadmap.

outputs.title: Broad established institutional Hub
outputs.summary: Demonstrate substantial journey coverage, enduring governance, product ownership and a prioritised ongoing roadmap.

outputs.title: Rationalisation evidence
outputs.summary: Identify redundant or competing entry points that can safely be consolidated or retired where replacement is proven.

steps.title: Continue product development and rationalise proven redundant entry points
steps.summary: After mobilisation, continue to deepen the Hub and progressively retire or consolidate redundant student-facing entry points where replacement functionality, service continuity and enduring ownership are proven.

outputs.title: Continuous product and rationalisation roadmap
outputs.summary: Operate the Hub as an enduring institutional product rather than treating the three-year mobilisation as a finished end state.

enablingConditions.condition: Confirm recurrent product, engineering, platform and support costs from live demand before transition into business as usual.
enablingConditions.owner: SED with Digital and IT and Finance
enablingConditions.decisionNeededBy: Before post-mobilisation recurrent budgets are fixed
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The Hub may enter business as usual without a sustainable operating model.
